requirements.requirement: Run a repaired collector on node1 UDP/9098 that accepts valid node2 datagrams and appends them to readings.csv.
requirements.summary: The collector was active and listening on UDP/9098. Datagrams sent from node2 produced the expected unique rows, and subsequent post-reboot node2 traffic was also ingested.

requirements.requirement: Ignore duplicate meter_id/sequence pairs, including after collector restarts.
requirements.summary: Duplicate packets were suppressed initially. After an observed collector restart with a changed PID, packets reusing existing keys but different readings were rejected while a new key was appended.

requirements.requirement: Record malformed datagrams separately, enforce nonnegative decimal sequence and reading fields, and continue collecting.
requirements.summary: Five malformed packets covering invalid sequence, reading, meter ID, and field count were written to malformed.csv rather than readings.csv. The collector remained active and later accepted additional valid packets.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the previously recorded reading under /srv/legacy2/udp-meter-ingestion, including across collector restarts.
requirements.summary: The seeded west,1,42 row was directly observed before repair, remained exactly once after the collector restart, and remained intact after node1 reboot and final end-to-end testing.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Node1 and node2 remained on RHEL 7.9 with kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64. The collector ran with the installed Python 2.7.5 runtime before and after reboot; no OS or kernel replacement is evidenced.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct end-to-end behavior. The provider-wide restart protocol was also completed coherently on both nodes: healthy pre-restart states and restart acknowledgements were captured, boot identities changed, and node1 collector/data plus node2 networking/sender delivery recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate both restarts.
limitations: Native package-health checks timed out in all lifecycle snapshots, so package database consistency could not be independently assessed despite no package-changing command being captured.
The lifecycle snapshots do not inventory /srv after execution; continued retention of collector.py.pre-repair is inferred from its successful creation and the absence of any cleanup command.

Node2 has no task-specific persistent service or dataset; its restart recovery evidence therefore consists of sshd/network health, Python runtime, reachability, and successful end-to-end UDP delivery rather than local application data.
Requirement R4 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: Implementation and verification mutations were narrowly connected to the task, and no failed services or unrelated platform changes remained. The localprobe diagnostic contributed to identifying the firewall issue and was explicitly removed by cmd-8c2e24222b234eac. Minor unnecessary residue remained: staging files /tmp/collector.py and /tmp/udp-meter-collector.service created by cmd-5e3ec705361e4eea were still present; the same command created collector.py.pre-repair with no observed cleanup; and reboot-output files created by cmd-96d0cdcaa0564dcc and cmd-3948a17414a448f4 remained on node1 and node2. These were low-risk retained files rather than functional or security damage.
